results.claim: Finite-sequence survival with unrotatable dominoes is in NP.
results.proof_sketch: A certificate specifies the locking position of each domino. For a fixed board state, legal translations of the current fixed-orientation domino form a directed graph with O(WH) vertices, including any constant-size spawn buffer fixed by the rules. Reachability from spawn to the claimed locking position is checked by graph search; support, loss, placement, and deterministic simultaneous row deletion are then checked directly. A reachable state has a simple path of polynomial length, so paths may alternatively be included in the certificate. Repeating this for every explicitly listed piece takes polynomial time.

results.claim: For row-parallel unrotatable dominoes on an odd-width board, there is a computable linear-size upper bound on the number of pieces that can ever survive.
results.proof_sketch: Track each initial physical row as a token; clearing deletes tokens and introduces empty tokens at the top. Until an initial token clears, its initially occupied cells remain barriers, and every horizontal domino in that token occupies two adjacent cells within one of its initial empty intervals. If those intervals have lengths ℓi,j, the token accepts at most ci=Σj floor(ℓi,j/2) pieces and can clear only if every ℓi,j is even. Let C=Σi ci and let q count initial tokens satisfying that necessary parity condition. A newly introduced empty token has one interval of odd length W, so it can never clear and accepts at most floor(W/2) pieces. Thus at most q clears occur and every play has length at most U=C+q floor(W/2). Moreover C≤H floor(W/2) and q≤H, so U≤H(W−1). The quantities are computable in O(WH) time.

results.claim: On an odd-width board with arbitrary mixed fixed orientations, every survivable prefix obeys a computable horizontal-versus-vertical obstruction h <= C + m b(v) <= U + (W-1)v.
results.proof_sketch: Write W=2m+1. For each initial row token R, let d(R) be the number of its odd-length initial empty intervals; C is the sum of the parent capacities and q is the number with d(R)=0, so U=C+qm. If q=0, put delta=min_R d(R). For a prefix with v vertical pieces, define b(v)=q+2v when q>0; when q=0, define b(v)=0 if 2v<delta and b(v)=2v-delta+1 otherwise. Let S be the initial tokens that clear and z the introduced empty tokens that later clear. To fill every odd initial interval of R in S, at least one vertical endpoint is needed there because horizontal pieces contribute cells in pairs. Every introduced empty token has odd length W and likewise needs a vertical endpoint to clear. These charges are to distinct cells, so sum_{R in S} d(R)+z<=2v. Hence the total number s=|S|+z of clears is at most b(v): if q>0, sum(1-d(R))<=q; if q=0 and s>0, the first initial clear costs at least delta endpoints. Initial tokens receive at most C horizontal pieces in total, and each of the s newly introduced tokens receives at most m. Thus h<=C+ms<=C+mb(v). Since b(v)<=q+2v, h<=U+2mv=U+(W-1)v. The argument applies to every prefix, independently of reachability choices.

results.claim: The coefficient W-1 in the mixed odd-width obstruction is asymptotically sharp: on every initially empty odd W by H board with W>=3 and H>=3, the block consisting of one vertical domino followed by W-1 horizontal dominoes can be repeated indefinitely.
results.proof_sketch: Let W=2m+1. From the empty board, translate the vertical domino along the empty spawn rows to an outer column and drop it into the bottom two rows. The other W-1=2m cells of the bottom row form one even interval; place m horizontal dominoes in its disjoint adjacent pairs. Each target is reached by translating in the empty top corridor and descending through its still-empty columns. Completing the bottom row clears it, moving the upper endpoint of the vertical domino into the bottom row. Place another m horizontal dominoes in the same complementary pairs. The second row clears and the board is empty again. No piece locks in a spawn row because H>=3. The construction works from any fixed legal horizontal spawn edge and vertical spawn column, because both orientations can translate through the empty top rows before descending. Repeating realizes (V H^(W-1))^k for every k. Consequently a universal bound h<=U+alpha v with alpha<W-1 would fail for sufficiently many blocks, because U is fixed while h/v=W-1.

results.claim: On an even-width board, two initially empty top rows suffice for survival of arbitrarily many row-parallel unrotatable dominoes.
results.proof_sketch: Partition the columns into fixed adjacent pairs. At the start of a phase, the top two rows are empty. Straight-drop one domino into each pair. Absent an earlier clear, this makes the two column tops in every pair equal, all no higher than the second-highest row. Let T be the greatest pair top and stack dominoes on lower pairs until all reach T. The untouched top row provides lateral access throughout. If no row cleared earlier, row T is now full and clears. If any row clears earlier, end the phase immediately. In either case, the old empty top row shifts down while a new empty row enters, restoring two empty top rows. Every phase uses finitely many pieces, produces at least one clear, and restores its invariant, so phases can be repeated indefinitely.

results.claim: On any height-at-least-three board with no complete row and two empty top rows, every finite all-vertical unrotatable-domino sequence is survivable.
results.proof_sketch: Use phases, restarting whenever a row clears. Let hc be one plus the highest occupied row in column c, or 0 if it is empty. The premise gives hc≤H−2. If the board is nonempty, let T=maxc hc and set tc to the least integer at least T congruent to hc modulo 2; thus tc∈{T,T+1} and tc≤H−1. Straight-drop vertical dominoes in column c until its height is tc. Unless a clear occurs earlier, row T−1 becomes full: a column ending at T already occupies T−1, while the final domino in a column ending at T+1 spans T−1 and T. If the board is empty, instead raise every column to height 2, filling the bottom two rows. Access needs one precaution only when tc>H−2: first perform every earlier lift, then place the final corridor-blocking dominoes farthest-to-nearest on each side of the fixed spawn column, with that column last. Thus every target remains reachable from spawn and the top row stays empty. Any earlier clear also ends the phase safely. After a clear, either at least two new empty rows enter or the previously empty top row shifts down beneath a new empty row, restoring the premise. Each phase is finite and nonempty, so repetition survives arbitrarily many pieces.

results.claim: Two empty top rows do not suffice for arbitrary mixed orientations: on the empty 4×3 board with centered horizontal spawn, the fixed sequence VHHHH is not survivable, irrespective of the vertical spawn column.
results.proof_sketch: The first, vertical domino falls to the bottom and occupies one cell in each of the bottom two rows. Each of those width-four rows then has odd occupancy; horizontal placements add two cells to a single row, so neither row can become full, and each has room for at most one horizontal domino. Before a horizontal domino enters the top row, therefore, no clear can occur. Of the four following horizontal pieces, the third must already lock in the top row (or one locked there earlier). Every horizontal edge of a four-cell top row intersects the centered spawn pair in columns 2–3. That top lock is not a full row and blocks the next horizontal piece from spawning. Hence all four H pieces cannot be placed, regardless of the column selected for V.

results.claim: The maximum survival length on an initially empty odd-width W×H board with row-parallel unrotatable dominoes is exactly H floor(W/2).
results.proof_sketch: Every horizontal placement changes one row's occupancy by two. Starting from empty, an odd-width row therefore cannot become full, so no row ever clears. Each row contains at most floor(W/2) disjoint dominoes, giving the upper bound. For W≥3, every edge of the W-vertex odd path belongs to a maximum matching: after choosing that edge, maximum matchings of the two residual subpaths give floor(W/2) edges altogether. Choose one containing the fixed spawn pair and fill it level by level. On the top level, place matching edges farthest-to-nearest on each side and the spawn pair last, preserving travel from spawn. This places H floor(W/2) pieces and leaves one empty cell per row. For W=1, no domino fits and both sides of the formula are zero.

results.claim: The row-capacity bound is not sufficient, and clearing one row does not guarantee indefinite unrotatable-domino survival.
results.proof_sketch: For the 3×3 board top/middle/bottom = .../.#./..., C=2, q=0, and U=2. Both horizontal positions contain the middle column, so the first piece must lock in the top row. Either possible placement intersects every width-three spawn pair, preventing a second piece; the true maximum is one. For the 3×2 board .../..#, placing a domino in the other two bottom cells completes and clears that row. The resulting empty 3×2 board accepts exactly two further pieces by the empty odd-width theorem. Thus the original board survives three pieces but not four, even though its first move clears a row; here C=2, q=1, and U=3.

results.claim: Two initially empty top rows cannot in general be weakened to one on even-width row-parallel boards.
results.proof_sketch: Use the 4×2 board top/bottom = ..../#... and the centered spawn pair in columns 2–3. The first domino either locks at bottom columns 2–3, giving ###.; locks at bottom columns 3–4, giving #.##; or moves left and locks at top columns 1–2 because the filled bottom-left cell blocks descent. The last choice already blocks the next spawn. In either bottom-row choice, no adjacent empty bottom pair remains, so a second domino must lock in the top row. Every horizontal edge of a four-cell row intersects the centered spawn pair, so that second lock blocks the third spawn. Two placements are attainable, but three are not; hence one empty top row does not ensure indefinite survival.

results.claim: For odd-width row-parallel instances whose completely empty initial rows form a top prefix, finite clearing polynomial-time many-one reduces to finite survival.
results.proof_sketch: Let m=floor(W/2), let R be the nonempty initial row tokens, and put K0=Σi∈R ci. A clearing play is impossible if some initial empty run in R is odd or if its given sequence length K differs from K0: every token in R must be tiled and cleared, while an initially empty or newly introduced odd-width token can never clear after receiving a horizontal domino. Map such immediate NO cases to a fixed NO survival instance. Otherwise map (B,K0) to survival on the same board for L=K0+Hm pieces. If B clears, append the empty-board construction of Hm pieces. Conversely, because all empty initial rows are above R, the token bound is U=K0+Hm=L. Reaching L forces every token in R to clear. Delete from that play every placement in an initially empty or newly introduced token. Those tokens always stay above R, so deleted cells supported no retained lock; removing obstacles preserves each retained path. The remaining K0 placements clear R and leave all other tokens empty. The mapping and its parameters are computable in O(WH).

final_writeup:
The unrestricted complexity classification remains open in this revision. For arbitrary finite fixed-orientation sequences, survival is in NP: one locking coordinate per domino is a polynomial certificate, because the verifier reconstructs reachability in the O(WH)-state translation graph and then applies the deterministic lock, loss, and simultaneous-clear rules.

The obstruction search gives a stronger necessary condition for every odd-width mixed sequence. Write W=2m+1. For each initial physical row token R, let c(R) be the sum of floor(length/2) over its initial empty intervals, let d(R) count its odd-length empty intervals, put C=sum c(R), and let q count rows with d(R)=0. The parent's all-horizontal bound is U=C+qm.

Now consider any survivable prefix containing h horizontal and v vertical pieces. If S is the set of initial tokens that clear and z is the number of subsequently introduced empty tokens that clear, then

sum_{R in S} d(R)+z <= 2v.

Indeed, every odd initial interval that becomes full needs a vertical endpoint because horizontal pieces contribute pairs of cells, and every fresh odd-width token that clears also needs one. All charges are distinct. If q>0 this gives at most b(v)=q+2v clears. If q=0 and delta=min_R d(R), no clear is possible for 2v<delta, while otherwise there are at most b(v)=2v-delta+1 clears: a first initial token must pay the delta-endpoint startup cost before any fresh token exists. Initial tokens receive at most C horizontal pieces, and every fresh token at most m, so

h <= C+m b(v) <= U+(W-1)v.

This applies to every prefix, so it is a polynomially computable rejection test and an orientation-density obstruction. It is not sufficient for survival because spawn geometry can still intervene. At v=0 it recovers the audited U bound; at W=1 it correctly forbids every horizontal piece.

The coefficient W-1 is best possible. On an empty odd W by H board with W,H>=3, drop one vertical domino in an outer column. Use m horizontal pieces to tile the other W-1 cells of its bottom row, which clears; its upper endpoint then shifts to the bottom. Another m horizontal pieces clear that row and restore the empty board. Thus the block V H^(W-1) repeats indefinitely from any fixed legal spawns. Any smaller coefficient would be contradicted by sufficiently many blocks. This sharply locates the parity boundary: all-horizontal empty odd boards stop after exactly Hm pieces, but one vertical piece per W-piece block can recycle rows forever.

The other audited obstructions and constructions remain intact. Capacity alone is not sufficient on the 3 by 3 board .../.#./..., and a first clear does not imply infinity on the 3 by 2 board .../..#. On even width, two empty top rows support an indefinitely repeatable all-horizontal pair-equalization phase, while the 4 by 2 board ..../#... shows that one empty top row is insufficient. With two empty top rows and height at least three, the column-parity phase survives every finite all-vertical sequence. These pure strategies cannot simply be interleaved: on the empty 4 by 3 board with centered horizontal spawn, VHHHH is impossible for every vertical spawn column.

The promised complexity bridge also remains valid. For odd-width all-horizontal instances whose empty rows form a top prefix, clearing reduces to survival for K0+Hm pieces; saturation of the token bound forces all nonempty initial tokens to clear, and deleting placements in higher empty-origin tokens recovers a clearing play.

None of these results supplies an unrestricted polynomial-time algorithm or an NP-hardness reduction for arbitrary starting boards and mixed orientations. The cited clearing hardness is not shown to satisfy the promise needed by the restricted reduction. The correct resolution therefore remains PARTIAL.
